verbalization: Chlorhexidine, when used off-label for denture stomatitis, is associated with an increased risk of gingivitis through a mechanism involving inflammatory mediators. The evidence suggests that chlorhexidine, which is typically used for its antimicrobial properties, may inadvertently promote inflammation in the oral cavity when applied to denture stomatitis. This inflammatory response could lead to the progression of stomatitis to gingivitis, as the condition becomes more severe or persistent. The observed relationship is supported by a hierarchical pathway where chlorhexidine is linked to denture stomatitis, which in turn is linked to gingivitis, indicating a potential causal or contributory relationship. The integration of these pathways highlights the importance of considering off-label uses in clinical settings, as they may contribute to the development of more severe oral conditions.
